title: Serviceability Status Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Serviceability Status Record within the Fleet Readiness and Sustainment Database. Consolidates serviceability, inspection, repair and parts status. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record consolidates four statuses into one readiness picture: which units are serviceable, which inspections are due, which repairs are open, and which parts are holding repairs up. The mission-capable rate is computed from counted units, so the headline number always traces back to a list.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: fleet units: 21. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. # Serviceability Status Record: compute the mission-capable rate from counted units.
